title: MSA/DPA exception scoring, auto-approve thresholds, and SQ triage playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Sales and Legal teams spend too much time negotiating routine MSA/DPA exceptions and answering Security Questionnaires (SQs). Goal: Create a playbook that scores exceptions, defines auto-approve thresholds, and prescribes an SQ triage workflow to reduce cycle time and improve consistency across deals. Scope: MSA/DPA liability/indemnity/customer data clauses, standard DPA addendum changes, common SQ asks (encryption, data residency, access controls). Out of scope: bespoke escrow/legal fund agreements and government-specific procurement clauses (handled by SLED team).
background: In Q4 2025 we observed a median contract negotiation time of 28 days for SMB and 46 days for mid-market deals where legal exceptions were requested. A qualitative audit of closed deals showed 60% of exceptions fell into 12 recurring patterns. Sales escalations for standard SQ items caused repeated pull on engineering and security SMEs. This playbook aims to operationalize a risk-based auto-approve model and a lightweight SQ triage so sales velocity increases while legal risk remains bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Defined exception taxonomy with scoring rubric (risk, value, frequency)
Auto-approve thresholds documented and integrated into contract intake flow for deals under $250k ARR
SQ triage flow documented with clear SME routing rules and SLAs (48h internal, 5 business days to customer)
Pilot with 3 AE teams completed and time-to-sign reduced by 30% in pilot cohort
Stakeholder sign-off from Legal, Security, Sales Ops, and Revenue Engineering
proposed_solution: 1) Create an exceptions matrix: map clause type -> risk score (0-10) -> suggested resolution (auto-approve / sales-approved / legal-reviewed). 2) Auto-approve rules for low-risk exceptions for deals < $250k and for repeat customers after initial legal sign-off. 3) SQ triage: automated intake form that classifies asks into 'Standard', 'Requires SME', 'Escalation' with links to canned answers and templates. 4) Embed playbook into Salesforce/CLM intake via a short decision API and generate recommended language for Legal or Sales to include in counters. 5) Analytics dashboard to track exception frequency, time-to-resolution, and legal throughput.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk of under-reviewing subtle high-risk exceptions if scoring is too permissive — mitigated by periodic audits and requirement for Legal monthly spot-checks
Operational load on Security SMEs during ramp — mitigated by canned answers and a rotating on-call SME for triage
Sales adoption friction if auto-approve is perceived as restrictive — mitigated via clear appeal route and SLA-backed review for exception overrides
Edge-case enterprise procurement clauses (e.g., escrow) remain high-touch and will require different routing; playbook will not try to auto-resolve these
